tagline: A loop of four towns in General John Stark's country.
intro: From downtown Goffstown, NH 13 runs west to New Boston. The loop turns north there on NH 77 and NH 114 to Weare, east on NH 77 to Dunbarton, and south on NH 13 back to Goffstown. The Piscataquog River keeps beside much of the way, and when the byway was designated in 2008, sections of the old railroad bed through Weare, New Boston and Goffstown had already become paths for walkers and bicycles.

The state motto credited to General John Stark comes from a toast he sent his old comrades when poor health kept him from a Bennington reunion. In full it read, Live Free Or Die, Death Is Not The Worst of Evils.

moments.title: New Boston
moments.text: The Molly Stark cannon, cast in 1743 and given by the general to the town's artillery company after Bennington, is on the town seal and is fired each Fourth of July.

moments.title: Weare
moments.text: In 1772, after the sheriff caught a Weare sawmill cutting the king's mast pines, Ebenezer Mudgett and twenty men beat him and his deputy at the Quimby Inn and ran them out on horseback.

moments.title: Dunbarton
moments.text: Stark spent much time at the Page homestead between the wars and later married Molly Page, and the 2008 byway plan listed the homestead and his son Caleb's statue.

sources.label: Southern NH Planning Commission, General John Stark Scenic Byway Corridor Management Plan
